fields.classes: School: Necromancy, Touch Spells, Ritual Caster, Witch (Valda)
fields.text:
This spell forges a mortal connection between yourself and a humanoid creature that you touch. A target creature must be present for the entire time of casting. If the creature is unwilling, it must make a Constitution saving throw to resist the spell's effects.
	For the duration, if you are reduced to 0 hit points, the target is also reduced to 0 hit points, and vice versa. This spell ends if you cast it again, or if you choose to dismiss it as an action.

Source:	Complete Witch p. 32 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Blackjack (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: House of Cards, House f Darts, House of Dice, or House of Roulette

When you cast a cantrip that requires a single spell attack roll and you don't have disadvantage on the roll, you can choose to roll with advantage. The attack automatically misses if the sum of the two rolled dice exceeds 21, and it is a critical hit if the sum equals 21.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 5 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Gontingent Cantrip (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: House of Cards, House f Darts, House of Dice, or House of Roulette

When you finish a long rest, you can spend 10 minutes performing a ritual to create a contingent cantrip. Cast a warmage cantrip that has a casting time of 1 action or 1 bonus action and doesn't deal damage. The cantrip doesn't take effect immediately, but instead it takes effect the next time you speak a specified command word (no action required). When you perform this ritual, choose whether the cantrip targets you, the nearest friendly creature, or the nearest hostile creature. The cantrip can't use other warmage tricks when it comes into effect.
	You can only have one contingent cantrip at a time. If you perform this ritual again, the previous contingent cantrip ends.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 5 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Magic Moment (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: moment to think cantrip

When you cast moment to think, you can choose to also stop time for a willing or unconscious creature you can see within 30 feet. The creature can take one of the actions permitted by the spell during your turn, and you can interact with one another while time is stopped. During this time you can exchange items, swap locations, take the Help action for tasks while time is stopped, attempt to stabilize a dying creature, or have a short conversation without eavesdropping or interruption.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Mystical Retort (HB)
fields.text:
You learn the vicious mockery cantrip, which doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.
	Additionally, when a creature you can see makes an attack roll against you, you can cast vicious mockery targeting that creature as a reaction. If the creature fails its saving throw, the cantrip imposes disadvantage on the triggering attack roll, instead of the creature's next attack roll, potentially causing the attack to miss.
	Once you cast this cantrip as a reaction, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Prismatic Cantrip (HB)
fields.text:
Once on each of your turns, when you deal force damage with a warmage cantrip, you can roll a d6 on the following table to change the cantrip's damage type for this casting. You can apply tricks to the casting as normal using the new damage type.
	Additionally, you can apply the trick corresponding to the rolled damage type, even if you don't know the trick. You can do so twice and regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

Prismatic Cantrip:
d6 | Damage Type | Warmage Trick
1 | acid | Corrosive Cantrip
2 | cold | Icy Cantrip
3 | fire | Explosive Cantrip
4 | lightning | Static Cantrip
5 | poison | Draining Cantrip
6 | thunder | Silent Cantrip

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Radiant Cantrip (HB)
fields.text:
Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell that deals acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, poison, or thunder, you can change the damage type to radiant. You can reroll one of the cantrip's damage dice and must use the new roll.
	The number of damage dice you can reroll increases by 1 when you reach 11th level (2 dice) and 17th level (3 dice).

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Residual Cantrip (HB)
fields.text:
When you cast a cantrip that deals damage and requires a single spell attack roll and you miss, you can channel some of the residual magic into a secondary beam of arcane energy as a bonus action. Make a ranged spell attack against a creature you can see within the cantrip's range. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 damage of the cantrip's damage type. This beam doesn't count as a cantrip.
	This damage increases to 1d8 when you reach 5th level, to 1d10 when you reach 11th level, and to 1d12 when you reach 17th level.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Capture (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 10th level Warmage (Valda), House of Go
You gain the following formation:

	Capture. You can use this formation when you and three or more allies that aren't incapacitated are adjacent to a hostile creature and surround it. You can determine this by placing an imaginary cube around the hostile creature. If you and your allies are adjacent to each side of the cube, the creature is surrounded.
	When you activate this formation, the hostile creature must make a Dexterity saving throw against your warmage spell save DC or be enveloped by chains of magical force and stunned for 1 minute. At the end of each of the creatures turns, it can make a Dexterity saving throw, freeing itself and ending this formation on a success.
	Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Chips Are Down (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 10th level Warmage (Valda), House of Roulette

When you expend one or more Chips of Fate to bet and lose at least one bet, you regain one expended Chips of Fate.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Dartmaster (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 10th level Warmage (Valda), House of Darts

When you cast a cantrip that allows you to make multiple ranged spell attacks, such as magic daggers or force dart using the Split Fire trick, and you miss with one or more attacks, you can reroll all of your misses.
	Once you use this trick, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Warmage Trick: Gauntlet Upgrade (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 10th level (Warmage), Coalition Arcanist

You install a high-power module in your blaster gauntlet. Whenever you cast a warmage cantrip using your gauntlet as the spellcasting focus, you can use one of the following warmage tricks. You can't use other warmage tricks when you use one of these tricks. Once you use one of these tricks, you can't use that trick again until you finish a long rest.

	Beam. When you cast a warmage cantrip that requires one or more spell attack rolls and deals damage, you can focus the cantrip into a 5-foot-wide, 60-footlong line. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your warmage spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d10 damage for each point of your proficiency bonus. The damage type is the same type that the cantrip deals. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. You can't use your Warmage Edge or Arcane Surge features when you use this trick.

	Overheat. The cantrip's damage dice become d12s.

Source:	Complete Warmage p. 6 (Indie)

fields.name: Drang's Morning After (HB)
fields.text:
Originally developed as a hangover cure by a suffering pirate, Drang's Morning After instantly cures the effects of poison on the target. The caster cracks an egg, which the target must consume raw, fueling the spell with small bits of abjuration magic that instantly soothes the stomach and head.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Bandits & Brigands p. 24 (Third Party)

fields.name: Pickpocket (HB)
fields.text:
You conjure a small, invisible conduit between your hands and a point within range, allowing you to reach through space and pilfer from afar. The conduit is intangible, undetectable by normal means, and large enough for your hands to pass through. You can use your action on each of your turns to attempt to steal a small object such as a pouch, scroll, potion, or similar item, from a creature you can see within the spell's range. The conduit can be moved up to 30 feet as a bonus action.
	When you attempt to steal from a creature, make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) or Intelligence (Arcana) check, contested by the target's Wisdom (Perception) check. On a success, you retrieve one unattended item the creature is visibly carrying (such as on their belt or in a satchel). On a failure, the attempt is noticed and the spell immediately ends.
	Items gripped or actively wielded cannot be taken using the spell.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Bandits & Brigands p. 24 (Third Party)

fields.name: Poisoned Blade (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (The fang of an adder)
fields.text:
You imbue one melee weapon with virulent magical toxins. For the duration, attacks made with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 poison damage on a hit.
	The first time each turn that the poisoned weapon hits a creature, that creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) or become poisoned for 1 minute. A poisoned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
	This spell has no effect on constructs, undead, or creatures immune to poison.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Bandits & Brigands p. 25 (Third Party)

fields.name: Lemmy's Giant Stride (HB)
fields.text:
Created to help the caster reach the window of a tower without being seen, this spell greatly increases the climbing and movement speed of the target. For the duration, the target of this spell's movement speed is doubled, and they gain a climbing speed equal to their movement speed. if the target already has a climb speed, it is doubled.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Bandits & Brigands p. 25 (Third Party)

fields.name: Brilliant Flash (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (A pinch of magnesium wrapped in cloth)
fields.text:
You speak a word of power and hurl the charged components toward your enemies, unleashing a searing burst of light and sound. Each creature within a 30-foot cube centered on a point you choose within range must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature is blinded and deafened until the end of its next turn. If the saving throw fails by 5 or more, the creature is also incapacitated for the same duration.
	A creature affected by this spell may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending all effects on itself on a success.
	This spell has no effect on creatures that are already blinded, defeaned, or both.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Bandits & Brigands p. 25 (Third Party)

fields.name: Thornskin (HB)
fields.text:
You touch a willing creature, and thorns grow from their body. Until the spell ends when a creature misses the target with a melee attack or hits with a natural attack, they take 1d4 piercing damage. The target's unarmed and natural attacks deal an additional 1d6 piercing damage.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 29 (Third Party)

fields.name: Create Vines (HB)
fields.text:
Choose a point within range, and a 30 ft. long and 5 ft. wide mat of vines extends from that point in a direction of your choosing. When grown over a gap, the vines count as a bridge. When the vines are grown up a wall, the surface can be climbed at a speed equal to your movement speed.

At higher-levels: When cast this spell using a 2nd level spell slot or higher, the length increases by 20 ft. and the width increases by 5 ft. for each slot level above 1st.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 29 (Third Party)

fields.name: Floral Barb-Shooter (HB)
fields.text:
A plant grows in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within range. The plant occupies that space and the flowers it grows contain sharp barbs that are expelled when prey gets too close.
	Any creature hostile to you that moves to a space within 20 feet of the Barb-Shooter must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. The creature takes 5 piercing damage on a failed save, or 2 piercing damage on a successful one. The plan wilts and vanishes when it has done a total of 40 damage.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 29 (Third Party)

fields.name: Tree Feller (HB)
fields.text:
A large tree suddenly grows and then falls, crushing and knocking down those in its path. Choose a point of origin within range. A 30 ft. line extends from that point in the direction of your choosing. Any creatures in that line must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or take 5d8 bludgeoning damage and fall prone, taking half damage on a successful save.

At higher levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th or higher level, increase the length of the line by 10 ft., and the damage by 1d8 for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Fantastic Flora p. 29 (Third Party)

fields.name: Avalanche (HB)
fields.components: S, M (A small barrel of alcohol worth at least 10 gold)
fields.text:
A wave of snow and ice shoots forth in a 30 ft. cone. All creatures within the cone must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, creatures take 3d6 cold damage plus 3d6 bludgeoning damage and are pushed 20 ft. away and knocked prone. On a successful save, creatures take half the damage and are otherwise unaffected.

At higher levels: When you cast this spell at 4th level or higher, the length of the cone increases by 5 ft. and the cold damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 3rd.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 35 (Third Party)

fields.name: Bounty of Apples (HB)
fields.components: V, M (A falcon feather and a nut)
fields.text:
Up to 10 magical apples appear in your hands. As an action, a creature can eat one of the apples, regaining 1d8 hit points. Additionally, the creature is resistant to piercing, slashing, and bludgeoning damage for one minute, and they do not age for that minute. Each apple provides enough nourishment for one day.
	The apples lose their magic if they have not been consumed within 24 hours of casting this spell.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 35 (Third Party)

fields.name: Edda of Heroics (HB)
fields.components: V, M (A master crafted instrument worth at least 1,000gp, which the spell consumes)
fields.text:
You begin reciting an epic poem that takes 1 hour to perform. The benefits of the edda don't set in until this hour is over. Up to twelve other creatures can gain the benefit of the edda.
	A creature that listens to the entirety of the edda gains several benefits. The creature gains 30 temporary hit points, becomes immune to the frightened and charmed condition, makes Constitution saving throws with advantage, and gains one inspiration. Those benefits last for 24 hours.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 35 (Third Party)

fields.name: Mistletoe Dart (HB)
fields.text:
A single dart of mistletoe shoots out like an arrow toward a target within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 6d4 piercing damage. This damage ignores resistances and immunities. If the target has resistance to piercing damage, increase the damage dice to d6s. If it has immunity to piercing damage, increase the damage dice to d8s. If the target is a celestial, fiend, fey, monstrosity, or undead, any successful attacks with this spell are considered critical hits.

At higher levels: When you cast this spell as a 4th level or higher, increase the damage dealt by 2d4 for each spell slot above 3rd.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly - Legends of Norse Mythology p. 36 (Third Party)

fields.name: Blight Spark (HB)
fields.text:
You hurl a mote of sickly energy that flickers like a dying candle. Make a ranged spell attack against a creature you can see within range. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 necrotic damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or emit dim greenish light in a 5-foot radius until the end of its next turn. While glowing, it can't benefit from invisibility.

At higher levels: The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach 5th level (2d8), 11th level (3d8) and 17th level (4d8).

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 28 (Third Party)

fields.name: Zealot's Brand (HB)
fields.text:
You mark a creature with a flickering brand visible only to allies. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be cursed for the duration. While cursed, the first attack made against the target each round has advantage.
	Additionally, any creature that hits the branded target regains 1 hit point per turn. This healing does not affect constructs or undead.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 28 (Third Party)

fields.name: Veil of the Unspoken (HB)
fields.text:
You draw a veil of whispered silence over the minds of your enemies. Choose one creature within range. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be muzzled by psychic interference. While muzzled:

	• The target cannot speak or cast spells with verbal components.
	• If the target attempts to speak, a shriek of gibbering voices erupts in its head, causing it to take 1d6 psychic damage.

The target may repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

At higher levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 28 (Third Party)

fields.name: Litany of Stillness (HB)
fields.text:
You speak a slow, rhythmic prayer. Choose up to three creatures within range. Each must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature's speed is halved and it cannot take reactions. If the target attempts to cast a spell, it must first roll a Constitution saving throw or lose the spell. On a successful save, the target is immune to the effect for the duration of the spell.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 28 (Third Party)

fields.name: Soulshackle (HB)
fields.text:
Choose two creatures you can see within range. Ghostly chains lash out from a rift between them. Each target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be soul shackled for the duration. While shackled:

	• When one target takes damage, the other takes half as much damage.
	• If either target is reduced to 0 hit points, the other must make a Constitution saving throw or fall unconscious for 1 minute.
	• A creature may use its action to repeat the Charisma save, ending the effect on a success.

Source:	GM Toolkit Monthly (Sinister Cult) p. 29 (Third Party)

fields.name: Invocation: Cloak of the Raven (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 15th level, Pact of the Cloak feature

You can use a bonus action on your turn to cause large, raven-like wings to sprout out of your cloak. While you wear the winged cloak, you gain a flying speed equal to your current speed. You can dismiss the wings using another bonus action.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Invocation: Ghost-Iron Chains (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 5th level, Pact of the Chain feature

Your familiar becomes ghostly in appearance, and gains the ability to become incorporeal. Your familiar can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but if it ends its turn inside an object it is immediately dismissed to its pocket dimension.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Invocation: Mantle of the Everlasting (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: Pact of the Cloak feature

You gain proficiency with medium and heavy armor.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Invocation: March of the Restless (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 5th level

You can cast animate dead using a warlock spell slot. You can do so twice, and regain both uses when you complete a long rest.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Invocation: Mirror Blade (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: Pact of the Blade feature

When you conjure a one-handed weapon as your pact weapon and have nothing in your other hand, you can conjure a shadowy copy of the weapon in your other hand. You can perform two- weapon fighting with these weapons, even if the weapons aren't light, and you can perform the somatic components of spells while both your hands are wielding your pact weapons. While the second weapon counts as magical, it does not inherit any magical properties from the weapon it was copied from.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Invocation: Pact of Blood (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 7th level

You can cast blood seal at will as a 2nd-level spell, without expending a spell slot or material components. You still need to pay the hemomancy cost as normal.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Invocation: Sanguine Seeker (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: eldritch blast cantrip

When you reduce a creature to 0 hit points with eldritch blast, you can cause the beam to continue through the creature, taking on a crimson hue. Select a new target within range and make a ranged spell attack against it. That creature takes force damage equal to any excess damage left over from the previous attack, plus an additional 1d4 necrotic damage.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

name: Invocation: Tales of the Crimson Tome (HB)

fields.name: Invocation: Tales of the Crimson Tome (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: Pact of the Tome feature

You can drop a pinch of humanoid blood into your book of shadows, and then ask one question aloud. Over the next minute, the blood manipulates itself into a language of your choice, answering your question in the process. The answer is provided using the knowledge of the humanoid that provided the blood, and is answered in less than 25 words. The blood must be from a living humanoid, and needs to be dropped into the book within a minute of it leaving the body.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Invocation: Veil of the Night (HB)
fields.text:
Prerequisite: 9th level, Pact of the Cloak feature

When you are wearing your pact cloak, you can use your action to turn invisible until the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until the end of your next turn.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 21 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Animate Blood (HB)
fields.classes: School: Necromancy, School: Hemomancy, Cleric, Sorcerer, Wizard
fields.text:
You animate droplets of your own blood to act under your command. For every three hit points spent in the casting of this spell, you create a droplet of animated blood
	As you cast the spell, and as a bonus action on each of your turns thereafter, you can mentally command the droplets to move as long as they are within 120 feet of you. The droplets have a speed of 30 feet, and a climbing speed of 15 feet.
	As an action on your turn, you can choose to see and hear from the location of one of the blood droplets until the end of your turn, becoming blinded and deafened to your own surroundings. Additionally, you may instead use your action to cause one of the droplets to explode in a burst of necromantic energy, destroying the droplet and damaging surrounding creatures. Each creature within 5 feet of the droplet must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 6d4 necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by 1d4 for each slot level above 3rd.

Hemomancy:
You must spend a number of hit points during the casting of the spell. Spending hit points in this way causes you to take necrotic damage equal to the amount spent, which cannot be reduced through any means. The number of hit points you can spend is based on the spell's level, and is shown in the table below. You may not use temporary hit points to cast hemomancy spells.

Hemomancy Spell Table:
Spell Level | Minimum Cost | Maximum Cost
1st | 1 | 10
2nd | 4 | 15
3rd | 7 | 20
4th | 10 | 25
5th | 13 | 30
6th | 16 | 35
7th | 19 | 40
8th | 22 | 45
9th | 25 | 50

When you cast a spell with the hemomancy tag, you must spend a number of hit points that is between the minimum and the maximum amount you can spend. For example, if you are casting a spell of 2nd level, you must spend at least 4 hit points to cast it, though you can choose to spend up to 15 hit points in order to increase the power of the spell.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Aura of Shade (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a deep black stone)
fields.classes: School: Illusion, Bard, Druid, Ranger, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You create a 15-foot radius sphere of shadow magic centered on a point within range. The area appears to be wreathed in swirling shadows and darkness, and is easily identifiable when it is in an area of bright or dim light. The sphere spreads around corners, and each creature that ends their turn within the area becomes invisible. This invisibility ends for a creature if they attack, cast a spell, or leave the area. Anything they are wearing or carrying is also invisible as long as they are.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Banshee's Wail (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (a strand of banshee hair)
fields.classes: School: Necromancy, Bard, Cleric, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You release a mournful wail that pierces into the mind of those that hear it. Each creature within 20 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d8 psychic damage, falls unconscious, and is deafened for 1 minute. On a success, it takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect. An unconscious creature wakes up after 1 hour, if it takes any damage, or if another creature uses its action to shake them awake. A deafened creature automatically succeeds on the save.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Beacon of False Life (HB)
fields.components: V, S, M (alcohol or distilled spirits)
fields.classes: School: Necromancy, Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
Necromantic energy emanates from you in a 30-foot radius area. Until the spell ends, the area moves with you, centered on you. While within the area, you and every creature that you have under your control (such as through an animate dead spell) gains 2d4 temporary hit points at the start of each of their turns. These temporary hit points last until they leave the area.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Blackblood (HB)
fields.classes: Monk (Way of the Bloodied Fist (HB)), School: Transmutation, School: Hemomancy, Cleric, Sorcerer
fields.text:
You transform a portion of your blood into a poisonous substance. As you cast this spell, you must spend a number of hit points. You gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the amount spent. For as long as these temporary hit points last, whenever a creature hits you with an attack while within 5 feet of you they take 1d8 poison damage and become poisoned until the start of their next turn.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, you gain 5 additional temporary hit points for each slot level above 1st.

Hemomancy:
You must spend a number of hit points during the casting of the spell. Spending hit points in this way causes you to take necrotic damage equal to the amount spent, which cannot be reduced through any means. The number of hit points you can spend is based on the spell's level, and is shown in the table below. You may not use temporary hit points to cast hemomancy spells.

Hemomancy Spell Table:
Spell Level | Minimum Cost | Maximum Cost
1st | 1 | 10
2nd | 4 | 15
3rd | 7 | 20
4th | 10 | 25
5th | 13 | 30
6th | 16 | 35
7th | 19 | 40
8th | 22 | 45
9th | 25 | 50

When you cast a spell with the hemomancy tag, you must spend a number of hit points that is between the minimum and the maximum amount you can spend. For example, if you are casting a spell of 2nd level, you must spend at least 4 hit points to cast it, though you can choose to spend up to 15 hit points in order to increase the power of the spell.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Blackflame (HB)
fields.classes: School: Transmutation, Bard, Cleric, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard
fields.text:
You choose a flame that you can see within range and that fits within a 5-foot cube. The flame momentarily changes color into a deep black, and then lashes out at surrounding creatures. Each creature within a 5-foot radius extending from the flame must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes 1d6 necrotic damage and 2d6 fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the necrotic damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

Source:	Dark Arts Player's Companion p. 25 (Homebrew)

fields.name: Bloodburn (HB)
fields.classes: Cleric (Blood Domain (Dark Arts) (HB)), School: Evocation, School: Hemomancy, Sorcerer, Wizard
fields.text:
You inflict a burning pain upon yourself, causing another creature that you can see within range to feel an even more excruciating pain as their blood boils. As you cast the spell, you must spend a number of hit points. The creature must then make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes 2d6 + the number of hit points spent as fire damage, and immediately falls prone as they become wracked with pain. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and doesn't fall prone. Constructs, elementals, and undead are immune to this spell.

At Higher Levels: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d6 for each slot level above 1st.

Hemomancy:
